newsitem.title: USA: Calif. personal bankruptcies at record high in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Calif. personal bankruptcies at record high in Q1.

text.p: A record number of Californians filed for personal bankruptcy in the first three months of this year, CDB Infotek, a public records information service, said on Friday.
First-quarter filings rose 6.2 percent to 48,779 from 45,948 in the previous quarter, and 30.9 percent from 37,263 in the first quarter of 1996, CDB said.
The numbers include bankruptcy filings under Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, the vast majority of which are personal filings, though some businesses are included.

Among reasons cited by analysts for the rise in bankruptcies are easy credit availability, an economic recovery which has not reached all segments of the population, and fewer negative consequences for those who file, it said.

Southern California accounted for more of the state's rise in bankruptcies than other regions. First-quarter filings rose 41.5 percent to 31,342 from 22,151 in the same period a year ago. Los Angeles County experienced a 71.9 percent year-over-year increase.

The San Francisco Bay Area filings rose 4.7 percent in the first three months to 7,344 from 7,017 in the year-ago quarter. In the Central Valley from Sacramento to Kern counties, filings climbed 21.5 percent rise to 6,950 from 5,721.
